html: The Hanis Coos are a Native people of Coos Bay on the southern Oregon coast. They spoke Hanis, one of two Coosan languages; the other, Miluk, was spoken by the Miluk Coos to the south. They fished salmon, gathered shellfish and camas, and lived in plank houses around the bay and the lower Coos River. Fur traders came in the 1820s and settlers in the 1850s. A treaty they signed in 1855 was never ratified, and they were held for years at Fort Umpqua and then at Yachats, where many died. Their descendants belong mainly to the Confederated Tribes of Coos, Lower Umpqua and Siuslaw Indians and to the Coquille.
